close_reason: MSRV 1.73 means trim_ascii unavailable; document as future improvement when MSRV bumps
description: NormalizedIter::new (lib.rs:1440-1453) manually computes start/end indices to strip leading/trailing spaces: 'let start = bytes.iter().position(|&b| b != b' ')...'; 'let end = bytes[start..].iter().rposition(...)''. In idiomatic Rust the standard library's trim_ascii (stable since 1.80) or the pre-1.80 pattern 'bytes.trim_ascii_start().trim_ascii_end()' expresses this more directly. As-is it is correct but more code than needed. Consider: 'let trimmed = bytes.trim_ascii(); Self { bytes: trimmed, pos: 0, pending_space: false }'. (Check MSRV: rust-version = 1.73, so trim_ascii is NOT yet available. Document that this is deferred to when MSRV bumps to 1.80+.)
title: pkix-path (rusty): NormalizedIter::new uses manual start/end index computation — use trim idiom
